title: The Patient Room
premise: Dominic Iversen returns to Hollow Creek to bury their twin brother, only to find the funeral was for the wrong body — and the real twin is still answering calls from inside the house. The town's founders bound something beneath the old patient ward with a harvest ritual, and every generation must feed it a pair of siblings or the town's dead come walking. As the photographs begin adding a chair that pulls people into it, Dominic uncovers that grandma Ida was the last keeper and that the town has been choosing its sacrifices for a century. To save what remains of their family, Dominic must finish the founders' interrupted ritual before the harvest moon rises — but the ritual demands a twin, and the thing wearing their brother's voice has other plans. In the end, Dominic completes the rite by offering the truth instead of blood, unbinding the town at the cost of forgetting their twin entirely, and walks out of Hollow Creek a stranger to their own grief.
about_author: Odile Sterling is the pen name of a former hospice night nurse who spent a decade writing down what patients said in their last hours. Her debut novella 'Count the Doors' won the Ashgrove Prize for quiet horror, and she lives in a farmhouse with more rooms than the deed allows.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body in the Casket
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic arrives in Hollow Creek for the funeral, but the body's dental records don't match their twin Elias — and the mortician refuses to open the casket twice. The town watches too closely, too kindly. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion as Dominic realizes the whole town may know something they don't.

chapters.title: Phone Calls from the Upstairs Room
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At Grandma Ida's house, Dominic's phone receives calls from Elias's number — static, breathing, and once, clearly, 'Dom, don't count the doors.' Ida's ledger of door-counts, kept nightly for sixty years, is found under floorboards. Emotional beat: dread replacing mourning; the house itself becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Old family photographs now show a plain wooden chair in the center of every room, and when Dominic looks directly at it in the newest photo, they find themselves briefly standing in the photo's kitchen, smelling Ida's bread. A neighbor, Ruth Calloway, warns: 'The chair picks the next pair.' Emotional beat: the horror becomes intimate and inescapable.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ruth Calloway. Ruth, last of the founders' line willing to talk, reveals the 1898 covenant: a ritual binding the 'Patient' beneath the old ward, fed every harvest by a sibling pair so the town's dead stay buried. Her own brother was taken in 1974. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth — Ruth has protected the lie her whole life and is finally breaking.

chapters.title: What Ida Kept
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Searching Ida's locked room, Dominic finds her keeper's journal: she was supposed to hand the ritual to the twins on their eighteenth birthday and never did, buying the town forty extra years with her own sister's memory. The chair in the photographs is getting closer to the camera each time. Emotional beat: anger at Ida's betrayal braided with love for her sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Waxes
chapters.summary: POV Elias (the thing wearing him). Locked in the upstairs room between door-counts, Elias's fragmentary consciousness narrates his slow consumption by the Patient, which offers him belonging in exchange for delivering Dominic. He resists, leaving clues in the phone calls. Emotional beat: tragic tenderness — the monster's hostage fighting from inside.

chapters.title: The Town That Chose
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic confronts the town council in the old patient ward and finds the ritual room beneath: a chair, a circle of names, and the founders' unfinished final verse. The council admits they've been selecting pairs for a century and want Dominic and Elias to complete it. Emotional beat: power's corruption laid bare — ordinary people justifying a hundred years of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Count the Doors
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On the eve of the harvest moon, the dead of Hollow Creek walk, and the house's doors multiply beyond counting. Dominic follows Elias's clues through the shifting rooms to the upstairs room where the Patient wears his face. Ruth dies holding the threshold open, her loyalty to her brother's memory finally spent. Emotional beat: terror at full pitch, love as the only compass.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Verse
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the ritual room, the Patient offers Dominic the one bargain that matters: Elias's life in exchange for binding themselves as the new keeper, alone, forever. Dominic instead speaks the founders' missing verse — the truth spoken aloud, the covenant named for what it is — and the circle of names begins to burn. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth; refusing the lie even to save a brother.

chapters.title: A Stranger to Grief
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The ritual completes at moonrise: the Patient unbound, the town's dead finally at rest — and the price is every memory of Elias, the truth-verse consuming what it named. Dominic wakes in a clean, chairless house with an empty room upstairs and a grief with no object. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — belonging purchased at the cost of the person who made them belong.
